small_guidance:
- The current kernel recomputes the conv output for every pool position (POOL*POOL=16x redundant work). Refactor so each program computes the conv output for the full pool window once into a small register tile (e.g. POOL×POOL per spatial output element), then reduces. This alone should cut work ~16x.
- Increase BLOCK_OC to 32 or 64 and reduce BLOCK_SP to 32 to better amortize weight loads across the GEMM-K dimension (IC*KH*KW=72); add a triton.autotune sweep over {BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_SP, num_warps∈{4,8}, num_stages∈{2,3}}.
- Hoist the weight load out of the pool loop — load w[oc, ic, kh, kw] once per (ic,kh,kw) and reuse across all POOL*POOL conv positions in the window.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an implicit-GEMM conv: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile of size POOL*POOL aligned to a pool window). Accumulate the full POOL×POOL conv tile in registers via a K-loop over (IC*KH*KW), apply tanh+scale+bias in the epilogue, then reduce-max across the POOL*POOL axis before the single store. This eliminates the POOL² redundant conv evaluations the current kernel does.
- Use channels-last (NHWC) layout for the input and weight so the GEMM-K reduction (IC) is the contiguous axis — load IC-vectors per (kh,kw) position with coalesced reads, and use tl.dot for the inner product when BLOCK_OC and BLOCK_K are tile-friendly.
- Consider persistent-CTA scheduling over (N*POH_tiles*POW_tiles) with each CTA owning a full OC slab so the weight tile (OC×IC×KH×KW=64×8×3×3=4608 floats = 18KB) stays resident in shared memory / registers across many output tiles.
